title: The God of Small Things
events_chronological: Ammu, divorced from a violent husband, comes back to her family's house in Ayemenem with her twins Estha and Rahel.
Ammu's aunt Baby Kochamma makes it plain that she resents both the twins and their mother.
Velutha, an untouchable carpenter, works at the family's pickle factory and is the twins' closest friend.
On the drive to meet their English cousin, a man behind a cinema refreshment counter forces Estha to masturbate him.
Sophie Mol arrives with her mother Margaret and is fussed over by the whole household.
Ammu and Velutha begin meeting at night on the far bank of the river.
Velutha's father tells the family about the affair.
Ammu is locked in her room and shouts through the door that the twins are millstones round her neck.
The twins and Sophie Mol row across the river in the dark, the boat overturns, and Sophie Mol drowns.
Baby Kochamma tells the police that Velutha abducted the children and raped Ammu.
The police beat Velutha to the edge of death in the derelict house across the river while the twins watch from a doorway.
Baby Kochamma makes Estha say that Velutha took them, and Velutha dies in a cell.
Estha is sent away to his father, and Ammu dies alone in a lodging house at thirty-one.
Rahel, divorced, comes back to the house in Ayemenem and finds it rotting with Baby Kochamma watching satellite television all day.
Rahel finds Estha, returned to the house years earlier, walking in the rain and no longer speaking at all.
Rahel goes to the derelict house across the river, now a heritage hotel where the old stories are staged for guests.
Rahel and Estha stand in the shut pickle factory where the vats used to be.
Rahel and Estha, alone in the house at night, sleep together.
syuzhet_notes: The novel alternates between the fortnight around the cousin's death and the return a quarter of a century later, drifting between them mid-paragraph. The present-day strand is told forward and so is the earlier one; the book closes on the earliest scene of the affair, so the last thing the reader is given is the beginning.
fabula_notes: Chronology is recoverable from the ages of the twins and from the cousin's death, which the novel dates precisely. The prose withholds the two central events - the drowning and the killing - until late, but never places them ambiguously.
